blocks.text: Why data scientists use Excel on Mac

Data scientists often need to perform quick sanity checks. Excel provides an immediate view of your data without requiring a full Python environment. You can filter, sort, and visualize small datasets in seconds. The Mac version of Excel supports most features found in the Windows version. You just need to know where to find them.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for data scientists
Efficiency comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Learning these shortcuts will reduce your reliance on the mouse.

Data cleaning is a large part of your work. Excel has built-in tools to help. You can remove duplicates using Data > Remove Duplicates. Use text functions like TRIM and CLEAN to handle messy strings. If you find data formatted as text, use the Text to Columns feature to force it into numeric format.
If Excel keeps removing leading zeros from your IDs, format the cells as Text before pasting your data. This prevents the automatic conversion to numbers.
blocks.title: Keep leading zeros

blocks.text: Excel handles over one million rows. However, performance drops as your sheet grows. Use Power Query for complex data transformations. It is more efficient than standard formulas. Always keep your raw data on a separate sheet. Perform your analysis on a copy to avoid data loss.

Pivot tables are your best friend for quick aggregation. You can drag and drop fields to find patterns. Use slicers to filter your data dynamically. For predictive tasks, use the Data Analysis Toolpak for regression and correlation. If you need to see how variables affect an outcome, try the What-If Analysis tools.

Formulas often fail when data is missing or incorrectly typed. Wrap your main formulas in IFERROR to return a clean value instead of an error code. Use XLOOKUP instead of VLOOKUP. It is more flexible and does not require the lookup value to be in the first column.

faq.question: Can Excel on Mac handle large data files?
faq.answer: Excel supports up to 1,048,576 rows. Large files may slow down depending on your Mac's RAM. Use Power Query for better performance.

faq.question: How do I speed up my work in Excel?
faq.answer: Learn keyboard shortcuts, use templates, and use Lazur to find tools quickly without digging through menus.

faq.question: Is Excel good for data science?
faq.answer: It is excellent for data exploration, quick visualization, and reporting. It complements Python and R for non-programmatic tasks.
